cipherprune.scope: Sections 3.2–3.3 and Appendix A threshold/count, stable full-record compaction and compacted-order degree disclosure. The original half-gates backend and explicit mixed garbled-decision/arithmetic-movement backend share exact Q16 numerics. Local-dealer OT and triples, client-local scoring and public thresholds replace distributed setup and learned policy. No selected-polynomial execution, trained checkpoint, causal-state mapping or provider transport.
cipherprune.result: The mixed pruning/top-k cohort checks 171,303 exact outputs across 33 fresh processes. Matched 4×16 partial pruning cuts combined material 83.60%, but empty/keep-all cases increase material and local time. Mixed 39×896 pruning executes with 13.09 MB keys and 8.39 MB peer frames across 688 serial rounds to retire 143 kB of two-party records. All possible counts must fit 64 MiB live allocation, 512 MiB cumulative keys and bounded products; 150-row worst-case admission rejects. The historical half-gates control separately checks 381 outputs in 15 processes and projects 631 MB evaluator material plus 106.60 MB client encodings at 39×896, failing admission. Count/degree disclosure remains explicit. Checkpoint quality, peak memory, full wire and decoder transport remain unknown. Details: docs/research/shared-selection-reference.md.

fastquery.scope: Sections 2.2 and 4.1–4.2 encrypted one-hot mixed-width packing, extracted-LWE output consolidation and signed packed-share conversion. Direct interleaving is a BumbleBee-derived alternative. Separate party input/output handles use a local random-OT dealer and half-gates, not distributed setup or SiRNN. Public W8A8-source requantization remains separate from fine-tuning and protected checkpoint execution.
fastquery.result: Eighteen fresh processes check 3,456 exact outputs. At 4,096×64 mixed precision, online HE/conversion frames fall 1,642,896 to 180,624 bytes with higher setup material and compute. Symbolic Qwen 39+32 still needs 234.32 MB online, 409.73 MB conversion keys and 1.76 MB setup per context (123.33 MB for 70 fresh contexts). Full-width noise and execution remain unvalidated. The historical requantization cohort still matches 10/12 prefill, 34/36 decode and 6/12 trajectories for mixed 4/3/3, with no exact logits/KV. The tied client head retains the same 136.13 MB matrix and releases zero weight bytes. Distributed setup, SiRNN, transport and whole-client memory remain open. Details: docs/research/packed-embedding-reference.md.

bumblebee.scope: Section IV/Figure 6 ciphertext-RNS normalization, trace and strided interleaving, used inside bounded encrypted embedding lookup. No BumbleBee whole-transformer, nonlinear, fine-tuning or production-transport reproduction.
bumblebee.result: Direct strided interleaving and extracted-LWE packing retain identical integer outputs and online frames in the eighteen-process 3,456-output lookup cohort. Direct interleaving performs fewer automorphisms for useful strided coefficients. Context/Galois setup, party-local conversion and table storage are counted separately; full-vocabulary noise and decoder execution remain unvalidated. Details: docs/research/packed-embedding-reference.md.

pcf-secret-replication.scope: Sections 4.1–4.2 two-party line PCF/SVMT with Remark 25 GGM puncturing and a full-field scalar/vector consumer. Local AES/dealer adaptation; restricted domains reject generic openings. No ring32 elementwise/FSS substitution, distributed setup or decoder execution.
pcf-secret-replication.result: Eighteen fresh processes check 5,778 exact modular outputs. At field 257 and 64 lanes, punctured keys reduce both-party raw material from 16,424 to 328 bytes; expanded correlations stay 1,032 bytes and peer frames 676 bytes. Worker expansion remains 65,664 combined field-output PRF evaluations. Exact restricted-mask and elementwise-reuse counterexamples prevent a generic nonlinear substitution. Symbolic full-field expansion at a near-32-bit prime exceeds one trillion PRF evaluations for 64 lanes and is not admitted. Peak memory, physical wire and Qwen costs are unknown. Details: docs/research/secret-replication-reference.md.

slalom.scope: Prepared masked linear and one-use trusted-client Freivalds verification. No enclave or attestation reproduction.

scorecard_components.scope: Related masked-linear method only. These lines do not select Slalom's Freivalds verifier or reproduce its TEE system.

slalom.result: Qwen2.5 native 100/40, one 50+8-token response per configuration: the verified adaptation takes 140.95 s and 374.00 MB TCP-stream traffic; composing exact codecs, demand issuance and paged compressed delivery gives 130.69 s and 334.21 MB. Client peak RSS falls 624.02 to 345.18 MB, while aggregate CPU rises 76.61 to 78.95 s. Outputs match; only same-verifier lines rank. Corrected native projection ownership removes the prior admission blocker. No TEE reproduction.

smoothquant.scope: Public per-channel equalization, fixed alpha=3/4, bounded scales and trusted-client activation scaling.
smoothquant.result: Pinned Qwen2.5: twelve held-out prefill prompts give 11/12 plain W8A8 versus 10/12 equalized top-1; top-5 stays 0.8833 and worst logit error improves 3.6207 to 2.5092. The 0.72953 MB profile uses eight public calibration sequences and covers 96 stages. A native 100/40, 50+8-token same-body pair reduces equalized latency 78.26 to 70.24 s, TCP-stream traffic 289.41 to 251.25 MB and client peak RSS 540.85 to 262.96 MB with exact codec/delivery composition; aggregate CPU rises 34.47 to 37.28 s. Outputs match on this cost prompt, but plain/equalized bodies rank separately. This is not a quality win; profile publication/distribution is extra.

curl.scope: Fig. 4/6 party-local shared lookup and public Haar compression, now composed with exact protected index/up/output rescaling and fresh Beaver multiplication in a bounded Q18-to-Q9 operator. Exact universal-interval helpers replace Curl's probabilistic truncation. No protected float conversion, Biorthogonal protocol, distributed issuance or decoder transport.
curl.result: The optional mixed arithmetic backend preserves the numeric profile but raises complete material 1.73x/4.15x for levels 0/4 and roughly doubles local online time. Hypothetical 39+8 combined material becomes 368.39/203.43 GB plus 35.38 GB peer frames. The shared 36-process, 2,916-output matched cohort includes six profiles and both backends. Fresh Qwen checks match 10/7 prefill, 34/34 same-token decode and 9/5 trajectories for levels 0/4; no logits/KV are exact. Each clear profile checks 128,876,544 integer outputs. Defaults and historical 213.08/49.06 GB cohorts remain separate. Trusted local issuance, exact conversion costs and decoder quality remain gates. Details: docs/research/mixed-gated-reference.md and docs/research/wavelet-gated-reference.md.

compact.scope: Complete Q18-to-Q12 SiLU × up with public-density-weighted dyadic Chebyshev fitting, private selection and exact half-gates rescaling/multiplication. Dyadic search, explicit tails and the Boolean backend adapt the paper's fitting/MPC contract. No tensor schedule or role transport.
compact.result: The optional mixed backend reduces combined material by 29.58/28.12/12.21% for four-piece quadratic/eight-piece cubic/sixteen-piece cubic profiles, and local online time by 55.57/51.79/35.95%. Explicit selection, random OT, arithmetic products and exact rounding still project 1.397/2.112/3.017 TB plus 123.33/145.37/145.37 GB peer frames at 39+8 geometry. The shared 36-process cohort checks 2,916 protected outputs. Fresh twelve-prompt Qwen results are 12/10/9 prefill, 35/36/34 decode and 8/9/7 trajectories, with no exact logits/KV. Each profile checks 128,876,544 independent integer outputs. These are PLLM adaptations, not Compact system costs. Historical Boolean cohorts remain in docs/research/compact-product-reference.md; matched follow-up: docs/research/mixed-gated-reference.md.

logrow.scope: Complete Q18-to-Q9 SiLU × up with the earlier two-row masked-index lookup and opaque half-gates rescaling/multiplication. Trusted client garbling, serial one-use lanes and final-only decoding. No compiler tensor schedule or provider transport.
logrow.result: The optional mixed backend replaces Boolean multiplication with an arithmetic product and explicit one-use conversions. Combined material falls 24.91% and local online time 15.24%, but hypothetical 39+8 material still needs 254.79 GB plus 33.81 GB peer frames. Garbling now belongs to a worker rather than the client; ownership and material delivery remain explicit. The shared 36-process cohort checks 2,916 protected outputs. A fresh twelve-prompt clear cohort matches 10/12 prefill, 34/36 decode and 9/12 trajectories; no logits/KV are exact and 128,876,544 integer outputs are checked. Default Boolean costs and original quality evidence remain in docs/research/logrow-product-reference.md. Follow-up: docs/research/mixed-gated-reference.md.

half-gates.scope: Native one-use Boolean half-gates, free XOR and bounded private selection/arithmetic circuits.
half-gates.result: Native circuit correctness and one-use tests; no independent cryptographic review or full-decoder benchmark.

garbling-gadgets.scope: Bounded CRT arithmetic garbling and Q7 multiplication adaptation.
garbling-gadgets.result: Primitive parity and material measurements only; no complete protected Qwen decoder score.

dash.scope: Bounded arithmetic-label and projection-gate adaptation; the paper's complete prepared convolutional network is not implemented.
dash.result: Bounded integer oracle and one-use tests. No whole-model cost comparison.

maverick.scope: Installed bounded RAA masked-matvec operator with client-owned P/Q preprocessing, fresh sparse sampling, one-use queries and post-response conditional checks. RAA distance and dual-LPN privacy remain uncertified; Walsh and Appendix E controls stay separate.
maverick.result: Historical native controls retain changed-output rejection and 48/96 admitted Qwen2.5 stage shapes. A separate fresh installed-SDK cohort checks 50,688 outputs in nine processes, with 51.72/66.45 MB client public payload on the admitted full-width shapes; both MLP shapes reject before allocation. Full-body P+Q still needs at least 22.90 GB. The cited q>2^31 distance-failure bound does not directly cover BabyBear. No admitted private/verifiable decoder or performance score.

carnival.scope: Attack against deficient public mask spans, following the later Maverick analysis. Carnival inference is not implemented.
carnival.result: Constructs bounded mod-2 leakage witnesses over u16/u24/u32 masks. An attack control has no inference-performance score.

scorecard_components.scope: DPF/GapARS/residual-SiLU primitives in CPU gated regions with trusted-client conversion and issuance. This is not SIGMA's GPU system or complete private decoder.

sigma.scope: Bounded early-terminated Boolean DPF, GapARS/TR floor shifts, residual Q12 SiLU and masked-wire multiplication. Public gap/effective-width bounds and one-use party-local state. Independent CPU/128-bit-seed implementation; no GPU system, protected float conversion or complete SIGMA decoder.
sigma.result: Twelve fresh processes check 5,136 protected block outputs. Complete keys are 645.25 bytes per party/element; 64 lanes use 6,020 peer bytes across eleven rounds. Qwen 39+8 geometry projects 6.93 GB combined material and 397.12 MB peer frames, versus the earlier numerically different 60.10 GB generic layout. Twelve fresh clear W8A8 trajectories match 10/12 prefill and 34/36 same-token decode selections, with 2.7158 worst logit error and no exact logits/KV. That historical cohort did not execute a protected checkpoint. A later unfused CPU two-worker SDK pair completes pinned Qwen2.5 at 30+2 tokens: serial/overlap takes 2,705.81/1,634.11 seconds with identical 5.72 GB TCP-stream traffic and outputs, nearly equal aggregate CPU and 227.20/229.49 MB client peak RSS. These client-converted gated regions do not establish complete SIGMA coverage or independent cryptographic review. Helper evidence: docs/research/interval-rescale-reference.md. Current scope and complete-response replay: docs/research/nonlinear-decoders.md.

grotto.scope: Internal suffix-parity comparison over early-terminated Boolean DPF keys; one child per level. Reused only within one bound lane/operation. No complete Grotto application or independent security review.
grotto.result: Exhaustive small domains and wide signed-boundary controls pass. Comparisons compose into the one-use masked-wire block's 5,136 checked outputs. This CPU implementation retains 128-bit seeds and separate controls, not SIGMA's packed 127-bit seed. No standalone paper performance score. Notes: docs/research/masked-wire-reference.md.

pika.scope: Boolean-DPF signed lookup with full-domain local evaluation, locally derived sign shares and fresh masked sign correction. Correlated corrections stay explicit; optional fresh party-local random-field seeding is a PLLM encoding adaptation. No complete Pika system.
pika.result: Every residual-table index passes independent integer checks at multiple masks; the lookup composes into 5,136 checked one-use gated outputs. The chosen 10-bit/40-bit lookup uses 726 bits per party per element. This operator cohort has no checkpoint execution, standalone speedup or reviewed cryptography. The helper also composes into the separate CPU masked-wire SDK response described in docs/research/nonlinear-decoders.md; that is not a Pika system reproduction. Operator notes: docs/research/masked-wire-reference.md.

fusefss.scope: Complete masked-wire gated-block multi-view fusion and the separate signed-rescale helper. Matched floor/Q12 layouts include lookup, multiplication, final rounding and fresh party-local material. Experimental CPU two-offset Experiments bind gated regions with client conversion/issuance and relayed peer frames; generated Qwen2/Qwen3 fixtures pass complete prefill/decode and SDK/gateway checks. Optional party-local random-field seeding is a PLLM encoding adaptation. Unfused dispatch has a real-checkpoint response pair; matched fused checkpoint costs, general fusion compilation and a GPU system remain absent.
fusefss.result: Eighteen fresh processes check 5,778 exact outputs. Multi-view fusion reduces complete-block rounds from eleven to eight and 64-lane peer frames from 6,020 to 5,552 bytes, but grows both-party keys from 82,592 to 145,984 bytes and local online time from 7.31 to 17.51 ms. The historical Qwen 39+8 geometry projects 6.93/12.25 GB unfused/fused keys and 397.12/387.30 MB peer frames. Both layouts share their numeric identity and remain benchmarkable despite negative local cost results. That operator cohort did not execute Qwen. The separate 30+2-token unfused serial/overlap SDK pair completes with 39.61% lower latency and unchanged 5.72 GB TCP-stream traffic; this is a scheduling gain, not a fused-layout win. Prior Q8/Q9 vector lookup, shared-Q7/helper and clear joint-output cohorts remain retained in docs/research/piecewise-gated-reference.md, docs/research/interval-rescale-reference.md and docs/research/joint-gated-reference.md. Primary-paper accounting caveats remain in docs/research/fss-paper-cost-audit.md. Current reproduction: docs/research/nonlinear-decoders.md.

fss-mixed.scope: Independent Figure 1 linear-size DCF and Section 4.1/Figure 14 public-boundary interval sharing over Z/(2^32), composed beneath one-use signed helpers. No mixed-mode compiler, reviewed transport or whole-decoder implementation.
fss-mixed.result: A k-bit comparator remains 20+22k bytes, but universal shifts let seven ties-even evaluations share at most three keys per one-use helper. Exhaustive masks/boundaries/closed intervals, full-width endpoints and lifecycle checks pass. Twenty-four fresh-process cases check 7,680 outputs. Fused 16/7 key payload drops 55.88% and issuance 55.25%; online work and peer bodies are nearly unchanged. Qwen helper keys still project 8.14 GB; review and complete-operator gates remain. Notes: docs/research/interval-rescale-reference.md.

nexus.scope: Independent Equation (4) CKKS exponential, encrypted reciprocal and complete normalization within fixed [-1/8,1/8] scores. Public shift and unrelaxed reciprocal iterations are PLLM adaptations. No secure maximum, attention QK/value products, masking, bootstrap or NEXUS system reproduction.
nexus.result: The two-profile cohort checks 738 outputs across 18 fresh processes, with worst softmax error below 3.21e-5. Only the client decrypts final outputs. Both methods consume fourteen levels; width-32 setup is 260.19 MB and three-row online frames 25.19 MB. Repeated-squaring local online median is 3.56 seconds. Independent Decimal profile and exp/sum errors remain separate. A fresh twelve-prompt pinned W8A8 audit rejects all 48 prefill/decode positions under this range, without executing an encrypted candidate (docs/evidence/research-encrypted-attention-range-qwen25.json). Historical [-16,16] rejection is preserved; no candidate-quality or whole-decoder claim. Notes: docs/research/encrypted-softmax-reference.md.

thor.scope: Independent Appendix C CKKS exponential and Algorithm 3 square/normalize with encrypted reciprocals and final normalization. Fixed [-1/8,1/8] range, delta1=1, delta2=2 and unrelaxed reciprocals are PLLM adaptations. No bootstrap, attention QK/value products, masks or THOR system reproduction.
thor.result: The two-profile cohort checks 738 outputs across 18 fresh processes, with independent Decimal profile and exp/sum oracles. Only the client decrypts final probabilities. Fourteen levels, 260.19 MB setup and 25.19 MB three-row online frames apply at width 32; square/normalize local online median is 8.38 seconds. Numeric profiles differ and cannot imply a general winner. A separate fresh twelve-prompt pinned W8A8 audit rejects all 48 prefill/decode positions under the fixed range, without executing an encrypted candidate (docs/evidence/research-encrypted-attention-range-qwen25.json). Historical range rejection is preserved; candidate quality and decoder execution remain unvalidated. Notes: docs/research/encrypted-softmax-reference.md.

mpcache.scope: Semantic KV eviction contracts, native selection and compiler-bound client-local static retention in ordinary Experiments. Native owners release discarded KV and preserve absolute positions. Historical client-garbled full-record/compact-index layouts bind owner revisions. A separate mixed selector admits complete 256-row/128-feature K/V under 15.45 MB live allocation, but uses 295.26 MB keys and 78.59 MB peer frames across 19,200 serial rounds to retire 131,584 clear-state bytes. Its scoring, live owner/revision binding and provider transport remain absent. See docs/research/shared-selection-reference.md and docs/evidence/research-shared-selection-cost.json. General dynamic/layer-shared MPCache and protected provider-held selection remain unimplemented.
mpcache.result: Fresh pinned Qwen W8A8 full retention preserves all 48 logit vectors and twelve final KV states. Median owned KV falls from 6.29 to 5.16 MB through capacity sizing. Keeping 75%/50% uses 3.90/2.62 MB but each matches only 35/36 decode selections, with no exact decode logits or final KV. Local-clear peaks remain 1.21–1.23 GB including body weights; diagnostic CPU rises. The static ClientLocalKv option completes ordinary SDK/gateway requests, retires buffers on completion/cancellation and re-prefills history follow-ups. Two fresh-client prepared SDK cohorts at 52/379 input tokens plus eight outputs under native 100/40 caps measure full-retention peaks of 257.77/524.85 MB versus dense 264.90/546.31 MB. Full output text matches; the longer 75% response changes text. Sparse retention does not monotonically lower peak RSS. Covered bodies stay 257.79/989.08 MB and latency is nearly unchanged. Each request passes runtime checks, but distinct numeric policies prevent rankings. The original longer workload's residue-frame failure is retained separately. These single-response cohorts establish neither broad quality nor 10x client-memory savings. SDK evidence: docs/evidence/research-retained-sdk-qwen25/short.json and docs/evidence/research-retained-sdk-long-qwen25/long.json. The historical full-backing oracle retains separate 8,712 equation checks and 34/36 static, 32/36 combined, 31/36 layer-shared selections. The first protected selection substrate checks 474 output words; sixteen two-feature rows cost 1.10 MB logical material plus 2.06 MB estimated metadata to retire 160 state bytes. A separate compact-index/full-gather comparison checks 4,041 words in 36 fresh processes, including 128-feature rows. Metadata falls but material rises in all five matched shapes; half-retaining 256 Qwen-width rows projects 1.77/8.71 GB per layer for full/compact layouts. Complete-state resource gates reject before issuance; provider-held scoring/state/transport remain unavailable. Evidence: docs/evidence/research-retained-selection-indices.json. Notes: docs/research/mpcache-reference.md.
